t.3.32.1: Then, in the midst of his ministers, Rāvaṇa, greatly enraged, questioned Śūrpaṇakhā, who was angry and speaking harsh words.
t.3.32.2: And who is Rāma, of what valor, of what form, of what prowess? And for what purpose has he entered the Daṇḍaka forest, so very hard to traverse?
t.3.32.3: And what is the weapon of Rāma by which the rākṣasas were slain, and by which Khara was slain in battle, and Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras as well?
t.3.32.4: Thus addressed by the lord of the rākṣasas, the rākṣasī, overcome with rage, then began to describe Rāma in due order.
t.3.32.5: Long-armed and large-eyed, clad in bark garments and the black antelope skin, and equal in beauty to Kandarpa, is Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
t.3.32.7: In battle I do not see the mighty Rāma taking up his terrible arrows, nor releasing them, nor drawing his bow.
t.3.32.6: Drawing his bow, which resembles the bow of Śakra and is adorned with golden bands, he shoots blazing iron arrows like deadly venomous serpents.
t.3.32.8: I see that army being struck down by showers of arrows, like an excellent crop beaten down by Indra with showers of hail.
t.3.32.9: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible prowess have been slain with sharp arrows by that one man, fighting alone on foot.
t.3.32.10: Within a muhūrta and a half, Khara was slain along with Dūṣaṇa, freedom from fear was granted to the sages, and the Daṇḍaka forests were made safe.
t.3.32.11: I alone was somehow let go, after being humiliated, by the great-souled and self-possessed Rāma, who shrank from the slaying of a woman.
t.3.32.12: And he has a brother of great splendour, equal to him in virtue and in valour, devoted and loyal to him, a mighty hero named Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.32.13: Intolerant of wrongs, hard to conquer, victorious, valiant, wise and mighty, he is Rāma's right arm, ever his very life-breath moving outside his body.
t.3.32.14: And Rāma's lawful wife, wide-eyed and illustrious, is named Sītā, a princess of Videha, with shapely hips and a slender waist.
t.3.32.15: Neither goddess nor Gandharvī, neither Yakṣī nor Kiṃnarī, nor any woman of such beauty have I ever seen before upon the face of the earth.
t.3.32.16: He whose wife Sītā would be, and whom she would embrace with delight, would live more gloriously than all others in all the worlds, even more than Puraṃdara.
t.3.32.17: She is of excellent character, praiseworthy in body, and unequalled in beauty on earth. She would be a fitting wife for you, and you likewise a fitting husband for her.
t.3.32.18: That fair-faced woman, broad of hips, with full and lofty breasts, I set out to bring here to be your wife.
t.3.32.19: But once you have seen Vaidehī today, her face like the full moon, you will become subject to the arrows of Manmatha.
t.3.32.20: If the desire arises in you to have her as your wife, then quickly let your right foot be raised here and set forth for victory.
t.3.32.21: O lord of the rākṣasas, do what is pleasing to those rākṣasas by slaying that cruel Rāma, who dwells in the hermitage.
t.3.32.22: Having slain him with sharpened arrows, and Lakṣmaṇa too, the great chariot-warrior, you will enjoy Sītā at your ease, as you please, once her protector has been slain.
t.3.32.23: If this speech of mine pleases you, O lord of the rākṣasas, then let my word be carried out by you without any hesitation, O Rāghava.
t.3.32.24: Having heard that the night-rangers stationed in Janasthāna have been slain by Rāma with his straight-flying arrows, and having learned that Khara and Dūṣaṇa too have been killed, you ought today to resolve upon what must be done.
